calls.headline: Local institutions absorb foreign selling as the EGX30 edges up
calls.body: The EGX30 rose 0.34% to 50,885.30 and the EGX70 EWI 0.09% on Tuesday, on EGP 8.8bn of turnover, 20.2% below the 90-day average (EnterpriseAM), with 109 stocks up and 88 down (Hapi Journal, Osoul Misr). Foreign institutions sold a net EGP 161.5m and Egyptian institutions bought EGP 167m (Youm7); by nationality, foreigners sold EGP 163.7m, Egyptians bought 126.6m and Arabs 37.1m (Youm7, Masrawy). Foreigners were 7.95% of trading. EFG Holding rose 2.0%, a fourth straight gain.
calls.view: The index is holding Monday's rebound on local money, not foreign: with futures pricing a December 9 Fed hike at about 96% and the 10-year Treasury at 4.91%, the extra return on Egyptian assets is shrinking for outside buyers, and Misr Life's book draws cash through November 30. The desk keeps its 48,000–53,000 range for the EGX30 into the IMF board vote; a hot PCE print today would test the low end first. Low confidence.
calls.wrong: The EGX30 closes below 48,000 or above 53,000 before December 15.
calls.notice: The split between institutions and individuals comes from one report (Youm7); the totals by nationality match Masrawy.

calls.headline: Suez Canal revenue doubles to $593m in November's first 24 days
calls.line: Returning carriers lift the canal's dollar income, a direct support for the pound.
calls.body: The canal earned $593m from 1,194 ships and 72m net tons between November 1 and 24, against $295m from 886 ships a year earlier, a 101.2% rise, Suez Canal Authority chairman Osama Rabie said (Business Today Egypt, Asharq Business, CNBC Arabia). Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd plan to bring three Gemini services back through the canal gradually from December to mid-January. The central bank's dollar rate eased to 54.17 buy and 54.31 sell on Wednesday morning.
calls.view: The pound's best news since the IMF staff deal: at this pace November earns about $740m, roughly double last year's, and the Gemini return brings back two of the largest container lines. It does not lift the EGX by itself, but it narrows the dollar gap a Fed hike would widen. The risk is the Red Sea itself: the Houthis threatened Saudi Arabia's Red Sea ports on Tuesday. Medium confidence.
calls.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 56 before December 15.

calls.headline: Misr Life's retail book fills a fifth on day one
calls.line: Retail investors ordered 7.1m of 37.5m shares; the institutional book, 95% of the deal, closes Friday.
calls.body: Retail investors ordered about 7.09m shares on Tuesday, the first day of Misr Life Insurance's offering, 0.19 times the 37.5m-share retail tranche and about EGP 96m at the top of the EGP 12.00–13.60 range (EnterpriseAM); no figures were given for the institutional book. The price is expected on November 28 and trading around December 3 (Zawya). EFG Hermes leads the deal.
calls.view: A slow first day says little: retail demand usually arrives near the close, and the deal lives on the institutional book. The desk still expects pricing in the upper half of the range, given the discount to BDO's EGP 13.82 fair value; a weak book would be a warning for the state's offering program. Small caps stay the side that pays while up to EGP 10.2bn is raised by November 30. Medium confidence.
calls.wrong: The shares are priced at the bottom of the range, or the EGX70 EWI rises more than 5% before November 30.
calls.notice: The 0.19 times figure is EnterpriseAM's, citing local press; no second outlet gave it.

calls.headline: A near-certain Fed hike narrows the bill trade's margin
calls.line: Futures put a December 9 hike at about 96% before today's PCE print, as foreigners sell Egyptian shares.
calls.body: CME FedWatch puts the odds of a quarter-point rise on December 9 at about 96% (BigGo, Herald Economy); the 10-year Treasury yield ended Tuesday at 4.91%. October PCE inflation and the third-quarter GDP estimate are due at 3:30pm Cairo, with core PCE expected at 3.2% from 3.1% (XTB). Egypt's one-year bill cleared at 26.16% on November 19, and overnight rates stand at 20% and 21% before the central bank's December 17 meeting.
calls.view: The carry trade still pays: a one-year bill at 26.16% against US yields under 5% leaves a wide gap, but every hike narrows it and makes a cut on December 17 less likely. That keeps banks' bill income high and keeps developers and other borrowers under pressure. The desk expects the central bank to hold on December 17. Medium confidence.
calls.wrong: The central bank cuts on December 17, or the one-year bill clears below 25% before then.
calls.notice: The PCE forecast comes from one outlet (XTB); the view does not rely on it.

calls.headline: Orascom Construction completes the OCI deal, nearly doubling its shares
calls.line: 97.2m new shares go to OCI's holders by December 8, lifting the count to 207.4m.
calls.body: Orascom Construction completed its purchase of OCI Rembrandt Holdings from OCI N.V., which holds OCI's former assets and liabilities, issuing 97,201,359 new shares and lifting its share count to 207,445,294 from 110,243,935 (Al Mal, Youm7). The shares go to OCI's eligible holders by December 8, once listed in Abu Dhabi and Cairo. The stock fell 0.9% to EGP 785.01 on Tuesday.
calls.view: The deal is done, so the risk is now supply: OCI's holders bought a fertilizer and chemicals company and receive shares of a contractor, and some will sell after December 8. The $11.6bn backlog, $4.8bn of it in the US, earns in dollars and should limit the damage; the desk expects the stock to hold above EGP 700 through the distribution. Low confidence.
calls.wrong: It closes below EGP 700 before December 31.

calls.headline: Analog Devices' 17.4% fall spreads the chip selloff past AI
calls.body: Analog Devices fell 17.4% to $312.95 on Tuesday, its worst day since at least 2003 (Trefis), despite record fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $4.37bn (Startup Fortune, 24/7 Wall St.); its first-quarter earnings guidance came in below forecasts and it plans $1.6–1.9bn of capital spending next year. Nvidia fell 5.9% to $155.38, Intel 8.1% to $54.80 and Broadcom 4.0% to $301.08, and the Nasdaq lost 1.48% to 23,733.54. Hewlett Packard Enterprise fell 16.3% after Wells Fargo cut its target to $50 (MarketBeat, Yahoo Finance).
calls.view: Monday's 31.5% Nvidia jump was relief over Huang's return, not new demand, and Tuesday shows the market now punishes chipmakers that beat but spend more or guide softer. With a Fed hike priced at about 96%, the desk expects the Nasdaq to stay below 25,000 into the December 9 decision. Low confidence.
calls.wrong: The Nasdaq closes above 25,000 before December 9.
calls.notice: Analog Devices' guidance and spending plan come from one outlet (Startup Fortune); the view does not rely on them.

calls.headline: The Dow tops 50,000 as money moves to retailers
calls.line: Dollar Tree's 11.2% jump lifted Walmart 2.1% as the S&P 500 fell for the eighth time in nine sessions.
calls.body: The Dow rose 0.85% to 50,018.70, its first close above 50,000, while the S&P 500 fell 0.50% to 7,201.09. Dollar Tree jumped 11.2% to $154.65, a three-year high, after third-quarter comparable sales rose 4.6% and traffic 3.8% and it raised its outlook (Trefis, Motley Fool); Dick's Sporting Goods rose 14.6% on results and a higher earnings outlook (company release, Motley Fool). Walmart rose 2.1% to $132.31 and Visa 1.8%.
calls.view: This is the rotation the desk has called since October 30: shoppers trading down help discounters, and a Fed hike favors companies that fund themselves from cash. Walmart's RSI above 70 says the run is stretched for now, so the gains may slow before they reverse. Medium confidence.

calls.headline: Oracle's credit swaps hit a record as AI borrowing costs rise
calls.line: Oracle fell 3.7% to $109.50 as five-year swaps at Oracle, Alphabet and CoreWeave hit records.
calls.body: Five-year credit default swap spreads at Oracle, Alphabet, SpaceX and CoreWeave reached records, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence figures reported by Reuters (Stocktwits via TradingView, Reuters via Yahoo Finance). Oracle fell 3.7% to $109.50, after rising 12.3% on Monday, and Alphabet 1.1% to $279.05.
calls.view: Credit is pricing the AI build-out's debt before equity does: wider swaps raise what Oracle and its peers pay to borrow for data centers, and a Fed hike adds to it. The desk expects Oracle to stay below $125 into the year end. Low confidence.

calls.headline: Sanofi buys Insmed for $41bn, lifting drug stocks
calls.line: Insmed rose 14.1% on a $175-a-share cash offer; Lilly gained 3.2%.
calls.body: Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for $175 a share in cash, about $41.0bn, adding the lung drug Brinsupri (Sanofi release, AJMC); Insmed rose 14.1% and Sanofi 9.7% in Paris. Kymera rose 15.7% after its eczema pill met its trial goals and it raised about $1.75bn in a share sale (MLQ.ai, TradingView). Eli Lilly rose 3.2% to $1,407.59 after Moody's raised its ratings to Aa2 from Aa3 (BigGo).
calls.view: Big drugmakers are paying cash for late-stage medicines, which supports biotech prices while tech sells off. Lilly trades on its obesity franchise, not on deals, and at 44 times trailing earnings leaves little room for a miss. Low confidence.
calls.notice: Moody's upgrade of Lilly is reported by one outlet (BigGo); the view does not rely on it.

drivers.name: New financing

drivers.name: A stronger dollar abroad

drivers.name: Record remittances
drivers.why: $13bn in July–September, up 20.4%, and $38.2bn in nine months, the economy's largest single source of dollars (central bank via EnterpriseAM).

drivers.name: Oil swings on Hormuz
drivers.why: Brent settled at $91.40 on Tuesday, up 2.3% on reports of ships hit near Hormuz, after touching $88.10, its lowest since late August; it slipped to about $87.50 on Wednesday morning (Moneycontrol).

view.headline: Suez dollars keep the pound in EGP 53–56
view.body: The pound firmed to 54.31 on Wednesday, within 2% of its strongest level in a year, as Suez Canal revenue doubled in November's first 24 days. The IMF board's vote on up to $2.3bn before December 15, record remittances and the canal's recovery should keep the dollar within EGP 53–56; a Fed hike at about 96% odds narrows, but does not close, the gap that one-year bills at 26.16% pay foreign holders.
view.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 56 before December 15, or the IMF board delays the review.
